requirement: A `{req}` opening fence MAY contain four or more colons. Habeas MUST accept opening fences of any length of at least three colons. A colon-only line with fewer colons than the opener MUST remain inside the requirement body, allowing a nested colon directive. A closing fence outside a fenced code example with at least as many colons as the opener MUST end the body.
rationale:
The reviewed tests cover every obligation in `requirements.ci.fence_lengths`. I judged this from the supplied test source alone and did not request implementation source.

**Obligations and the tests that cover them**

1. **Openers of four or more colons are accepted, at any length of at least three.**
   - `src/evidence.rs#mod[tests]/fn[validates_four_or_more_colon_fences_and_longer_closers]` runs openers of 4 and 7 colons through `validate_repository`. It asserts one requirement is found and the report has no errors.
   - `src/lib.rs#mod[tests]/fn[a_longer_colon_fence_contains_a_shorter_nested_directive]` checks that `definition_blocks` returns one closed requirement block for a `::::{req}` opener.
   - `src/fenced.rs#mod[tests]/fn[markdown_fences_close_with_enough_colons_and_skip_code]` checks a `::::{cite}` opener.
   - Three-colon openers are used throughout the fixtures.
   - `src/evidence.rs#mod[tests]/fn[example_bodies_keep_nested_markdown_and_trim_outer_whitespace]` covers 4- and 6-colon openers for `{example}`.

2. **A colon-only line with fewer colons than the opener stays in the body, so a nested colon directive works.**
   - In the 4-, 7- and 4-colon cases above, a nested `:::{note}…:::` sits inside the body. The tests assert the body text, or the requirement text recorded in the evidence JSON, includes the nested block and the text after it ("Still in the requirement.").
   - `src/lib.rs#mod[tests]/fn[a_longer_colon_fence_contains_a_shorter_nested_directive]` asserts the exact body range, `Intro.\n\n:::{note}\nNested.\n:::\n`, and that "Outside." falls after `end`.
   - `src/fenced.rs#mod[tests]/fn[markdown_fences_close_with_enough_colons_and_skip_code]` asserts that an inner `:::{impl}` and its `:::` stay in the outer body. It also asserts that a `::: trailing` line and an indented `    :::` line stay in a three-colon body.

3. **A closer with at least as many colons as the opener ends the body.**
   - The tests use equal closers (4/4) and longer closers (4/5, 7/8, 4/5 and 6/7 for examples).
   - Text after the closer ("Outside the requirement.") is not part of the body.
   - `src/fenced.rs#mod[tests]/fn[markdown_fences_close_with_enough_colons_and_skip_code]` also closes on `   :::::  `, a closer with surrounding whitespace.

4. **A closing fence inside a fenced code example does not end the body.**
   - `src/evidence.rs#mod[tests]/fn[colon_requirement_span_includes_markdown_and_excludes_following_text]` puts `:::` inside a ```` ```text ```` block in a requirement body. It asserts the full body, including the later heading text, is the requirement text and that validation has no errors.
   - The example test puts `:::{example} literal` inside a code block. It asserts that no `rules.literal` definition is created and that the body is preserved.
   - The `src/fenced.rs` test asserts that a directive inside a code fence is skipped when code is skipped, and is seen as ordinary text when it is not (4 fences versus 3).

**Gaps**

I found no gap. The boundaries the text names are all exercised: equal-length closer, longer closer, shorter nested colon line, and a code-fenced colon line. Each is asserted with exact body or text checks, and the tests carry `{test}` references to the requirement.
